[http://www.foodista.com/recipe/KD2PYYBV/fresh-tomato-galette Originally posted to Foodista] by Ala Lemon. Foodista recipes are released under a [http://www.foodista.com/static/legal CC-BY license].

==Ingredients==
*1 sheet [[Cookbook:Puff Pastry|puff pastry]]
*5 [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] powder
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] panko or fine dry [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|breadcrumbs]]
*3 tbsp freshly-grated [[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|Parmesan]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]], beaten

==Procedure==
#Preheat your [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200°C (400°F).
#Slice the tomatoes to 0.5 cm (¼ inch) thick, and set aside.
#In a bowl, combine 2 tbsp grated Parmesan with the thyme and mustard powder.
#Line a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking tray]] with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] and lay your puff pastry on top.
#Spread 2 tbsp panko or breadcrumbs, leaving about 4 cm (1½ inch) of the border uncovered.
#Sprinkle the cheese mixture evenly on top.
#Starting at the centre, arrange the tomato slices in concentric circles, overlapping each other.
#Sprinkle the remaining breadcrumbs and Parmesan on top, season with a little pepper if you like, and carefully fold the leftover dough over the tomatoes.
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] the galette with the beaten egg, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for about 30–40 minutes or until the dough is cooked through and golden brown.
#Allow the galette to cool down slightly before decorating with fresh basil leaves, and serve.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Roger Mooking suggests serving with [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], if you like.

steps.text: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
Slice the tomatoes to 0.5 cm (¼ inch) thick, and set aside.
In a bowl, combine 2 tbsp grated Parmesan with the thyme and mustard powder.
Line a baking tray with parchment paper and lay your puff pastry on top.
Spread 2 tbsp panko or breadcrumbs, leaving about 4 cm (1½ inch) of the border uncovered.
Sprinkle the cheese mixture evenly on top.
Starting at the centre, arrange the tomato slices in concentric circles, overlapping each other.
Sprinkle the remaining breadcrumbs and Parmesan on top, season with a little pepper if you like, and carefully fold the leftover dough over the tomatoes.
Brush the galette with the beaten egg, and bake for about 30–40 minutes or until the dough is cooked through and golden brown.
Allow the galette to cool down slightly before decorating with fresh basil leaves, and serve.
